glosses.notes: Used when something is made bigger in size, scale, or effect, whether it is a picture, a map, or even a problem.

examples.sentence: 老师把活动路线图放大以后贴在门口，怕第一次来的家长站在后排还是看不清明天集合的地点。
他没有把这个问题放大，先问了问来的人，再看大家最在意的到底是什么。
旧照片本来很小，工作人员把人脸部分慢慢放大，大家这才认出站在最后面的原来是年轻时候的校长。

example_translations.translation: After enlarging the activity route map, the teacher posted it by the door because she was afraid the parents coming for the first time still would not be able to see tomorrow's meeting point clearly from the back row.
He did not magnify this one problem. He first asked the people who had come and then looked at what everyone cared about most in the end.

The old photo was originally very small, so the staff slowly enlarged the part with the faces. Only then did everyone recognize that the person standing in the back was the principal when he was young.

glosses.notes: Most often used for letting birds, balloons, or similar things go into the air, and it can also extend to letting the mind or imagination go free.

examples.sentence: 公园做活动的时候，工作人员把养好的鸟一只一只放飞，周围看的人虽然很多，可是现场一直特别安静。
婚礼结束时，新人把写好名字的气球一起放飞，连站在后面的老人都一直抬头看到看不见为止。
活动最后，孩子们把手里的气球一起放飞，连站在门口的老师也抬头看了很久。

example_translations.translation: During the park event, the staff released the birds one by one. Although many people were watching, the whole scene stayed unusually quiet.

At the end of the wedding, the couple let the balloons with their names written on them fly together, and even the elderly people standing in the back kept looking up until they disappeared from sight.
At the end of the event, the children released the balloons in their hands together, and even the teacher standing at the doorway looked up for a long time.

glosses.notes: Describes something happening extremely fast, often with a sense of sudden momentum or a surprisingly quick change.

examples.sentence: 消息一传开，来买的人就飞速多起来，老板每天下午都得重新安排第二天卖什么。
山里的路一修好，快递从县里送到村里的时间就飞速缩短，很多年轻人这才愿意回来开网店。
消息一传开，来的人就飞速多起来，门口排队的人从早到晚一直没有断过。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the news spread, the number of buyers grew at high speed, and every afternoon the owner had to rearrange what to sell the next day.

Once the mountain road was repaired, the time it took deliveries to go from the county to the village shrank at high speed, and only then were many young people willing to come back and open online shops.
As soon as the news spread, people started coming in at high speed, and the line at the entrance never really broke from morning until night.

glosses.notes: Can describe something as fatty or thick, can mean gaining weight, and in farming it can also refer to fertilizer.

examples.sentence: 市场里卖鸡的老板一边挑一边说，这几只鸡看着不大，可是肉紧、油也不多，吃起来不会觉得太肥。
春天种地以前，村里先把肥送到地边，怕后来车太多，一忙起来就来不及了。
出院回家以后他照了照镜子，才发现自己这段时间又肥了一点。

example_translations.translation: While picking chickens at the market, the seller said that these birds did not look large, but the meat was firm and not too oily, so they would not taste overly fatty.
Before spring planting, the village first moved the fertilizer to the edges of the fields, afraid that later there would be too many vehicles and once everyone got busy, it would be too late.
After leaving the hospital and returning home, he looked in the mirror and only then realized that he had gotten a little fatter again during that time.

glosses.notes: Describes someone or something as clearly overweight, often in medical, health, or public discussion contexts.

examples.sentence: 医生说他已经有点肥胖，再不多走路、少吃一点，后面连上楼都会越来越累。
这只狗原来特别爱动，后来主人长期把零食放在手边，它一点一点变得肥胖，连上楼都不愿意了。
节目请来的教练提醒家长，不要把儿童肥胖只看成吃得多的问题，睡眠和运动时间其实一样重要。

example_translations.translation: The doctor said he was already somewhat obese, and if he still did not walk more and eat a little less, even climbing stairs would become more and more tiring later on.
This dog used to be especially active, but later its owner kept snacks within easy reach for a long time. Little by little it became obese and eventually did not even want to go upstairs.
The coach invited onto the program reminded parents not to see childhood obesity only as a matter of eating too much. Sleep and exercise time are just as important.

glosses.notes: Usually describes land or soil that is rich enough to support strong plant growth.

examples.sentence: 这片河边的土地一直很肥沃，所以村里很多人虽然去城里工作了，春天还是会回来把地先种上。
老人常说这里以前没有现在这么热，山上的水更多，下面那几块最肥沃的田一年能收两次。
这块地这么肥沃，所以村里的人年年都来这里种菜，到了秋天常常一车一车往外送。

example_translations.translation: The land along this river has always been fertile, so although many people from the village have gone to work in the city, they still come back in spring to get the fields planted first.
The older people often say it was not this hot here before and there used to be more water in the mountains, so the most fertile plots below could be harvested twice in one year.
This land is so fertile that people from the village come here to grow vegetables every year, and by autumn they often send them out cart after cart.

glosses.notes: The organ used for breathing. It often appears in health advice, medical explanations, and warnings about smoke or illness.

examples.sentence: 医生把片子放在灯下，指着左边的肺慢慢解释，说现在最重要的不是着急工作，而是先把咳嗽控制住。
医生告诉他，肺要慢慢恢复，所以刚不抽烟那几天，上楼还是会觉得累。
医生说他的肺还没有完全好，所以一闻到做饭的烟就容易咳，最近别急着上夜班。

example_translations.translation: The doctor placed the scan under the light and pointed to the left lung while explaining slowly that the most important thing now was not rushing back to work, but getting the cough under control first.
The doctor told him that the lungs recover slowly, so in the first days after he stopped smoking, climbing stairs would still feel tiring.
The doctor said his lungs had not fully recovered yet, so as soon as he smelled cooking smoke, he would easily start coughing, which was why he should not rush back onto the night shift just yet.

glosses.notes: A lung infection that is more serious than an ordinary cold and often comes up in hospital, recovery, and family care contexts.

examples.sentence: 孩子起初只是咳嗽，家里人都以为过两天就好，后来烧一直不退，去医院一查才知道已经是肺炎。
医生说老人这次肺炎好得慢，不只是因为年纪大，也因为前一阵子一直没有休息好。
宿舍有人得了肺炎以后，大家才认真把窗户打开通风，晚上也不敢再一直把门关着。

example_translations.translation: At first the child was only coughing, and everyone at home thought it would get better in a couple of days. Later the fever would not go down, and only after a hospital check did they learn it was already pneumonia.
The doctor said the elderly man was recovering slowly from pneumonia this time not only because he was older, but also because he had not been resting well for a while before that.
After someone in the dorm got pneumonia, everyone finally started opening the windows seriously for ventilation, and at night they no longer dared keep the door shut the whole time.

glosses.notes: Used when people split tasks and responsibilities so a group can work more clearly and efficiently.

examples.sentence: 活动开始前，班长先把大家叫到一起分工，谁去借桌子，谁去接老师，谁最后留下来收东西都说得很清楚。
这家小店虽然人不多，可是厨房和前台分工一直很细，所以中午最忙的时候也很少有人等太久。
他们第一次一起做活动的时候越忙越乱，后来把分工说清楚，谁做什么都定下来，事情才顺。

example_translations.translation: Before the event began, the class monitor first gathered everyone together to divide the work, making it very clear who would borrow tables, who would pick up the teacher, and who would stay behind at the end to pack things up.

Although this small shop does not have many staff, the division of labor between the kitchen and the front counter has always been very detailed, so even at the busiest time at noon, people rarely have to wait too long.

The first time they ran an event together, the busier they got, the messier it became. Later, once they explained the division of work clearly and fixed who would do what, things finally went smoothly.

glosses.notes: Used for sorting people, materials, or problems into different levels, grades, or categories.

examples.sentence: 医院把排队的人按情况先分级，不是为了谁重要谁不重要，而是怕真正着急的人一直等在后面。
这套阅读材料没有按年级直接排，而是先按难度分级，让刚来的学生也能慢慢找到合适的起点。
平台准备上线新功能以前，先把可能出现的问题分级，再决定哪些要连夜处理，哪些可以等第二天。

example_translations.translation: The hospital first classified the people waiting in line according to their condition, not because some mattered more than others, but because they were afraid the people in real urgency would be left waiting in the back.
This set of reading materials was not arranged directly by school year. Instead, it was graded by difficulty first so that students who had just arrived could slowly find a suitable starting point.
Before the platform launched its new feature, it first classified the problems that might appear, then decided which ones had to be handled overnight and which could wait until the next day.

glosses.notes: Can refer to dividing payment into installments or carrying out a project stage by stage instead of all at once.

examples.sentence: 他原来想一次把电脑买下来，后来算了算房租和车费，还是决定分期，这样每个月压力不会一下子太大。
这家医院没有一次全改完，而是分期做，先把最急的地方修好，再一块一块往后改。
销售人员讲合同的时候反复提醒，虽然可以分期付款，可是每一期的时间和金额都要提前写清楚。

example_translations.translation: He had originally wanted to buy the computer in one payment, but after calculating rent and transport costs, he still decided to pay in installments so the pressure each month would not become too heavy all at once.
This hospital did not renovate everything all at once. Instead, it did it in stages, fixing the most urgent places first and then changing the rest piece by piece.

While explaining the contract, the salesperson kept reminding them that although payment by installments was possible, the timing and amount of each installment had to be written down clearly in advance.

glosses.notes: Can describe people or things as spread out, or mean actively spreading them out so they are not concentrated in one place.

examples.sentence: 景区出口太窄的时候，工作人员会先把人群分散到几条不同的路上，免得后面一下子全堵住。
大家原来都坐在前面那几排，后来老师发现后面一直空着，就让同学们分散一点坐，方便小组讨论。
村里的住户比较分散，所以送快递的人每次进山以前都要先把路线记好，不然一个下午也跑不完。

example_translations.translation: When the scenic area exit becomes too narrow, the staff first scatter the crowd onto several different paths so that everything does not suddenly jam up behind them.
Everyone was originally sitting in the first few rows, but later the teacher noticed the back had stayed empty, so she asked the students to spread out a little to make small-group discussion easier.

The households in the village are fairly dispersed, so every time the delivery worker heads into the mountains, he has to memorize the route first. Otherwise even a whole afternoon is not enough to finish the run.

glosses.notes: Refers to the feeling a place, event, or interaction creates around the people in it.

examples.sentence: 这家小店地方不大，可是大家说话都不急，所以朋友第一次来就觉得这里的氛围很舒服。
会议一开始大家都不太敢说话，后来经理先把自己的失误讲出来，整个房间的氛围才慢慢放松下来。
旧照片和音乐一放出来，大家就觉得这里的氛围像以前一样，连说话的声音都慢了下来。

example_translations.translation: This little shop is not large, but nobody speaks in a rushed way, so the first time my friend came, he immediately felt the atmosphere here was very comfortable.
At the beginning of the meeting, nobody really dared to speak. Later the manager first talked about his own mistakes, and only then did the atmosphere in the whole room slowly relax.
Once the old photographs and the music were played, everyone felt the atmosphere here was like the past, and even the sound of people speaking seemed to slow down.

glosses.notes: Most often means fine powder, but it can also describe a light pink color in everyday speech.

examples.sentence: 她先把糖压成粉，再一点一点放到刚做好的点心上，怕一下子放多了会太甜。
她挑墙面颜色挑了很久，最后没有选太白的，而是留了一点粉，这样下午进门的时候看起来更暖。
她挑了一件有点粉的外套，穿到窗边一看，才发现颜色比店里看着更暖。

example_translations.translation: She first crushed the sugar into powder, then added it little by little onto the freshly made pastries, afraid that if she put on too much at once, they would become overly sweet.

She spent a long time choosing the wall color. In the end, she did not choose one that was too white, but kept a touch of pink so the room would feel warmer when people walked in during the afternoon.
She chose a coat with a slight pink tone, and only after wearing it by the window did she realize the color looked warmer than it had in the shop.

glosses.notes: Describes strong anger, especially when someone feels something unfair, careless, or harmful has happened.

examples.sentence: 听完那个年轻人被反复推来推去的经历以后，排队的人都很愤怒，觉得窗口至少该先给一个清楚说法。
父亲平时很少当面发火，可是看到有人在河边乱倒垃圾时，脸上的愤怒一下子就压不住了。
她没有立刻把愤怒写进公开回复里，而是先把事情经过从头整理好，免得情绪盖过真正的问题。

example_translations.translation: After hearing how that young man had been pushed back and forth repeatedly, the people waiting in line were all angry and felt that the service window should at least give a clear explanation first.
Father rarely loses his temper in front of people, but when he saw someone dumping garbage by the river, the anger on his face suddenly could not be held back.
She did not immediately pour her anger into the public reply. Instead, she first sorted out the whole sequence of events from the beginning so that emotion would not cover up the real issue.

glosses.notes: Used when an area, road, entrance, or space is shut and people are no longer allowed to enter it freely.

examples.sentence: 暴雨刚停，管理处就先把靠山那条小路封闭了，因为石头还在往下掉，谁也说不准什么时候才完全安全。
入口已经封闭了，所以工作人员一直站在门口提醒后面来的人别再往里走。
医生说伤口已经没有大问题了，但这几天还要继续保持封闭处理，别总想着拆开看看恢复得怎么样。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the heavy rain stopped, the management office first closed off the path by the mountain, because rocks were still falling and no one could say for sure when it would be completely safe.
The entrance had already been closed off, so the staff kept standing at the doorway reminding the people coming from behind not to keep going inside.

The doctor said the wound was no longer a major problem, but for the next few days it still needed to be kept closed in treatment, so there was no need to keep thinking about opening it up just to check how it was recovering.

glosses.notes: Refers to the visible natural or local scene that people enjoy looking at, especially while traveling or sightseeing.

examples.sentence: 车子刚转过那个山口，前面的湖和村子一下子都露出来，第一次来的游客常常还没下车就先拍风光。
他原来只想在海边住两天，后来觉得这里风光太好，白天看山，晚上听海，结果多留了一周。
墙上那几张老照片拍的是小城风光，所以很多老人一眼就认出了那条街。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the car turned past that mountain pass, the lake and village ahead suddenly opened up, and first-time visitors often start taking pictures of the scenery before they even get out of the car.

He had originally wanted to stay by the sea for only two days, but later felt the scenery here was too good to leave, with mountains to look at by day and the sea to listen to at night, so he stayed an extra week.
The few old photos on the wall showed the scenery of a small city, so many elderly people recognized that street at a glance.

glosses.notes: Can refer to the strength of the wind itself or to wind as a source of power in weather and energy contexts.

examples.sentence: 海边风力太大，工作人员下午就通知小船早点回来，别等天黑以后再走。
这片空地看起来没人注意，可是工程师连着站了几个月，才确认这里的风力稳定到可以装新的发电设备。
山上风力太大，送货的人常常得改时间，不敢按平常的速度开。

example_translations.translation: Because the wind force by the sea was too strong, the staff told the small boats that afternoon to return early and not wait until after dark to set out again.

This open area looks like the kind of place nobody notices, but the engineers observed it for several months in a row before confirming that the wind power here was stable enough to install new generating equipment.
The wind force in the mountains is too strong, so delivery drivers often have to change their timing and do not dare drive at their usual speed.

glosses.notes: Used when crops or produce come in especially well after a growing season.

examples.sentence: 今年天气好，地里的菜大多丰收，所以村里的人从早到晚都在忙着往车上搬。
春天那几场雨一来，大家就知道今年多半会丰收，所以还没开摘就先把车找好了。
大家一说今年丰收，站在地边装菜的人都笑了，连后面来帮忙的孩子也跑得更快了。

example_translations.translation: The weather has been good this year, and most of the vegetables in the fields have had a good harvest, so people in the village have been busy loading them onto vehicles from morning until night.
Once those spring rains arrived, everyone knew this year would probably bring a good harvest, so they arranged the vehicles before the picking had even started.
As soon as people started talking about this year's good harvest, the people standing by the field loading vegetables all smiled, and even the children helping in the back started running faster.

glosses.notes: Can refer to actual stormy weather, and by extension to the hardships people pass through over time.

examples.sentence: 山里的天气变得很快，导游刚说完前面那段路还能走，风雨就一起压下来，大家只好先退回旁边的服务站。
这家小店跟着老街经历了很多年风雨，门脸换过几次，老板也老了，可是每天清早还是第一个把灯打开。
父母一路经过那么多风雨，最常跟孩子说的不是吃过多少苦，而是有事先别急着怪别人。

example_translations.translation: Weather in the mountains changes quickly. The guide had only just said that the stretch of road ahead was still passable when wind and rain came down together, and everyone had no choice but to retreat first to the service station nearby.

This small shop has gone through many years of hardships along with the old street. Its storefront has changed several times and the owner has grown old, but every early morning he is still the first one to switch on the lights.

After going through so many hardships, what my parents most often tell their children is not how much they once suffered, but that when something happens, they should not rush to blame other people first.

glosses.notes: Used when someone gives time, effort, skill, or even a whole career to a cause, a group, or other people.

examples.sentence: 退休以后他没有闲下来，而是每周固定去社区图书馆帮孩子看书，大家都说这种长期奉献比一次捐钱更难。
医生说这份工作不轻松，可是能把时间和本事都奉献给最需要的人，他一直觉得很值。
节目没有把她拍成只会吃苦的人，而是让观众看到，她这些年把时间都奉献给乡村教育以后，自己也慢慢得到很多力量。

example_translations.translation: After retiring, he did not settle into idleness. Instead, he went to the community library every week to read with children, and everyone said that this kind of long-term devotion is harder than making a one-time donation.
The doctor said this job is not easy, but being able to devote both his time and his skills to the people who need them most has always felt worthwhile to him.

The program did not film her as someone who only knows how to endure hardship. Instead, it let viewers see that after devoting her time to rural education over these years, she herself gradually gained a great deal of strength.

glosses.notes: Can mean someone's wife, and in formal settings it also works as a respectful way to address or refer to a woman as madam.

examples.sentence: 晚会开始前，主持人先请那位先生和夫人入场，后排第一次来的人这时才知道他们已经到了。
大家一说起那位教授，总会提到夫人，因为家里来人多的时候，最会照顾人的就是她。
那位先生和夫人一到门口，前面等的人就过去打招呼，怕他们在外面站太久。

example_translations.translation: Before the evening event began, the host first invited that gentleman and his wife to enter, and only then did the people in the back who were there for the first time realize that the pair had already arrived.
Whenever people talk about that professor, they always mention the wife as well, because when many visitors came to the house, she was the one who knew best how to take care of everyone.
As soon as that gentleman and his wife reached the entrance, the people waiting in front went over to greet them because they were afraid the pair would have to stand outside too long.

glosses.notes: In everyday written use, this verb often means taking medicine. In other contexts it can also mean obeying or accepting someone's authority.

examples.sentence: 医生让他先连续服三天药，再看晚上咳嗽会不会减轻，所以他连出差都把小盒子按时间装好了。
这种药一天服两次，早晚各一次，医生怕他记不住，还在袋子上又写了一遍。
奶奶怕记错，就把早晚各要服几片写在纸上，这样一看就不会忘。

example_translations.translation: The doctor told him to take the medicine for three days in a row first and then see whether the nighttime cough would ease, so he even packed the little box by schedule when he went on a business trip.
This medicine is taken twice a day, once in the morning and once at night. The doctor was afraid he would not remember, so he wrote it out once more on the bag.
Grandma was afraid she would remember it wrongly, so she wrote down how many tablets to take in the morning and at night, and that way she would not forget once she looked at the note.

glosses.notes: Used when something rises or stays on the surface, and it can also extend to problems or thoughts gradually coming into view.

examples.sentence: 河水退了以后，边上还浮着一些木头，大家看见了就先拿到岸上，怕后面又堵住。
清晨湖面上还浮着一层雾，远处的小船开得很慢，站在岸上的人一时都没说话。
会议结束以后，真正的问题才慢慢浮出来，大家这才发现原来不是时间不够，而是前面的分工一直没定清楚。

example_translations.translation: After the river water receded, some pieces of wood were still floating along the edge, so when people saw them, they first carried them up to the bank for fear that things would get blocked again later.

Early in the morning, a layer of mist was still floating over the lake surface, the small boats in the distance were moving very slowly, and for a moment the people standing on the bank did not say anything.

Only after the meeting ended did the real problem slowly surface, and only then did everyone realize that the issue was not a lack of time, but that the division of work earlier had never been clearly settled.

glosses.notes: Used when someone follows orders, arrangements, or unified direction rather than acting only on personal preference.

examples.sentence: 消防演练不是比谁跑得快，而是看大家能不能在听到指令以后立刻服从安排，不往已经封住的出口挤。
新来的队员起初总想按自己的办法来，后来吃过几次亏才明白，在复杂现场先服从统一指挥比个人经验更重要。
他并不是没有意见，只是到了真正要执行的时候，还是会先服从决定，等事情结束再把建议一条一条提出来。

example_translations.translation: A fire drill is not about seeing who can run the fastest. It is about whether everyone can obey the arrangements immediately after hearing the instructions and not push toward an exit that has already been closed off.

At first the new team member always wanted to do things his own way, but after losing out a few times, he came to understand that in a complicated situation, complying with unified command matters more than personal experience.
It is not that he has no opinions. It is simply that when the time comes to carry something out, he still obeys the decision first and only raises his suggestions one by one after the matter is over.
